important_findings.title: First ownership search ignores snapshot observations
important_findings.reproduction: Clone actual report. Remove old-panel target_destroyed from original position, set at=2026-10-20T17:33:34.000Z and insert immediately before first new-panel target_info_changed at 17:33:34.908Z. Put the exact final new panel target into first poll_transition.targets at 17:33:33.194Z. All entry timestamps remain monotonically ordered. Retain later matching events and final snapshot. verifyHostedMemberDataLifecycleReport returns true and proof basis correlated_panel_materialization.
important_findings.why_real: Native capture snapshot() records exact owned target classifications via the same describe() as target events. Its worker-retirement polling starts immediately after click_resolved and can observe targets before the old panel destruction event. A snapshot already showing the replacement is ownership evidence; ignoring it while counting a later info-change launders the forbidden earlier materialization. No fresh global blank-node requirement is assumed.
important_findings.required: Derive earliest matching owned appearance across target events AND target snapshots; ensure all observed first-appearance evidence satisfies retirement order/time. Add a coherent snapshot-first real-report mutant.

additional_observations: Malformed first matching event timestamp is accepted because Date.parse(...)=NaN makes <= false, and a later valid event supplies afterRetirement.some. The current producer uses ISO timestamps, so this is recorded as defensive evidence-validation weakness rather than a separate product-realistic blocker.

A later trace matching event with a timestamp before retirement is accepted; the algorithm checks timestamp only on first event by array order. This contradicts a strict earliest-in-both-orders interpretation, but requires timestamp/trace disagreement and is not the primary finding.
